# DesignComplexSurvival

DesignComplexSurvival computes the operating characteristics of
two-group time-to-event trials analysed with the log-rank test, without
patient-level simulation:

- each group follows a four-state model (progression-free, progressed,
  switched, dead) with piecewise constant intensities, covering
  progression-free survival, overall survival and treatment switching at
  or after progression, with the post-progression intensities measured
  from progression or from randomization;
- accrual is piecewise uniform (by rates or by proportions) and dropout
  is piecewise exponential by group;
- expected events, the mean, variance and covariance of the log-rank
  statistic over calendar time, group sequential bounds by alpha and
  beta spending (binding or non-binding futility), power, type I error,
  and the number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up
  for a target power;
- progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) can be
  tested together with a group sequential fixed-sequence or Bonferroni
  procedure, with analyses driven by the events of either endpoint or by
  calendar time; the joint distribution of the two log-rank statistics
  gives the power of each endpoint, the probability of rejecting both or
  at least one hypothesis, and the familywise error rate.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival")
```

## Examples

A delayed treatment effect: the hazard ratio is 1 for 6 months and 0.65
afterwards. The number of events for 90 percent power with interim
analyses at 50 and 75 percent of the events:

``` r

library(DesignComplexSurvival)
lam <- log(2) / 12
scn <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_model(death = lam, dropout = 0.003),
  treatment = ms_model(time = c(0, 6), death = c(lam, 0.65 * lam), dropout = 0.003),
  accrual = ms_accrual(time = c(0, 3), rate = c(10, 30))
)
ms_size(scn, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 0.75, 1)),
        test = ms_test(futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD", param_fut = -2),
        power = 0.9, solve_for = "events", n = 700)
#> Solved for the final number of events: 587.802 (target power 0.9)
#> 
#> Group sequential log-rank design
#>   Tested endpoint: OS; looks driven by OS events
#>   Sample size: 700; accrual duration: 25.33; final analysis at: 58.66
#>   Power: 0.9001
#>   Type I error: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.02482 (binding)
#>  look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower hr_lower
#>     1 25.45    294      0.50   2.963 0.001525   0.7078 -0.5039   1.0605
#>     2 35.51    441      0.75   2.359 0.009162   0.7988  0.7166   0.9340
#>     3 58.66    588      1.00   2.014 0.022000   0.8469  2.0141   0.8469
#>  prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>     0.06203    0.02689   0.06203
#>     0.46398    0.02760   0.52601
#>     0.37413    0.04536   0.90014
```

PFS and OS tested together: PFS and OS are exponential in both groups
(the model of Fleischer et al. 2009), with medians of 4 and 12 months in
the control group and 6 and 16 months in the treatment group. PFS is
tested at 300 PFS events, where OS is also tested, and OS again at 220
OS events. OS is tested only after PFS has been rejected (fixed
sequence):

``` r

fl <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 4, median_os = 12),
  treatment = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 6, median_os = 16),
  accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25)
)
ms_power(fl, n = 450,
         looks = ms_looks(c("pfs", "os"), fraction = c(1, 1),
                          test = list(c("pfs", "os"), "os")),
         test = ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "fixed_sequence"),
         events = c(pfs = 300, os = 220))
#> Group sequential log-rank design with two endpoints
#>   Endpoints: PFS, then OS (fixed sequence, overall); looks driven by PFS events and OS events
#>   Sample size: 450; accrual duration: 18; final analysis at: 23.05
#>   Power: PFS 0.9387, OS 0.5452; both 0.5452; at least one 0.9387
#>   FWER under global null: 0.025 (non-binding), 0.025 (binding)
#>  endpoint look  time events info_frac z_upper  p_upper hr_upper z_lower
#>       PFS    1 18.62    300    1.0000   1.960 0.025000   0.7975   1.960
#>        OS    1 18.62    163    0.7407   2.357 0.009207   0.6912    -Inf
#>        OS    2 23.05    220    1.0000   2.009 0.022243   0.7626   2.009
#>  hr_lower prob_upper prob_lower cum_power
#>    0.7975     0.9387          0    0.9387
#>        NA     0.2966          0    0.2966
#>    0.7626     0.2486          0    0.5452
```

## Validation

The tests compare the results with an independent Python implementation
(`inst/validation/python/`, using matrix exponentials and adaptive
quadrature) and, when the packages are installed, with gsDesign,
gsDesign2, rpact and lrstat.

The scripts in `inst/reproduce/` recompute sample sizes, numbers of
events, analysis times, bounds and powers printed in 14 sources
(articles and a statistical analysis plan). The scripts in
`inst/validation/` compare the package with patient-level simulations of
8 scenarios (FastSurvival and a Python simulation; PFS and OS analysed
together in 4 of them), with the covariance estimator of Danzer et
al. (2025) applied to large simulated trials under the null hypothesis,
and with the package PWEALL in 8 designs. Each folder is run by its
`run_all.R`, which judges every value as PASS (the criterion is met),
EXPLAINED (the criterion is met after a registered explanation, such as
an apparent misprint), FAIL, or INFO (not judged: a published value
computed by a method that the package does not reproduce, or an
asymptotic approximation compared with simulation):

| Folder             | PASS | EXPLAINED | FAIL | INFO | Total |
|:-------------------|-----:|----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|
| `inst/reproduce/`  |  243 |        75 |    0 |  191 |   509 |
| `inst/validation/` |  849 |         0 |    0 | 1366 |  2215 |

`run_all.R` also multiplies the compared values by 1.1 and checks that
the judgements change as expected. The criteria are described in the
`README.md` of each folder and the registered explanations in its
`explained.csv`. Every compared value is listed with its judgement in
`results/summary.csv`, and `results/summary.md` summarizes the results.
FastSurvival and PWEALL are needed only to rerun `inst/validation/`.

# Package index

## Model and scenario

- [`ms_model()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_model.md)
  : Multistate model for one treatment group
- [`ms_fleischer()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_fleischer.md)
  : Exponential model for PFS and OS of Fleischer et al. (2009)
- [`ms_accrual()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_accrual.md)
  : Piecewise uniform accrual
- [`ms_scenario()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_scenario.md)
  : Two-group trial scenario
- [`ms_null()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_null.md)
  : Null scenario

## Endpoint distributions

- [`ms_surv()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_surv.md)
  : Survival function, hazard and density of an endpoint
- [`ms_prob()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_prob.md)
  : State occupation probabilities

## Events and the log-rank statistic

- [`ms_events()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_events.md)
  : Expected numbers of patients, events and dropouts over calendar time
- [`ms_event_time()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_event_time.md)
  : Calendar time at which a number of events is expected
- [`lr_moments()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/lr_moments.md)
  : Mean and variance of the log-rank statistic over calendar time
- [`lr_cov()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/lr_cov.md)
  : Joint distribution of the log-rank statistic at several calendar
  times

## Group sequential bounds and probabilities

- [`gs_spend()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/gs_spend.md)
  : Error spending functions
- [`gs_bounds()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/gs_bounds.md)
  : Bounds of a group sequential design
- [`gs_prob()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/gs_prob.md)
  : Stopping probabilities of a group sequential design
- [`gs_prob_mtp()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/gs_prob_mtp.md)
  : Rejection probabilities of a group sequential design with two
  endpoints

## Design

- [`ms_looks()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_looks.md)
  : Timing of the analyses
- [`ms_test()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_test.md)
  : Test and stopping rules
- [`ms_power()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_power.md)
  : Power of a group sequential log-rank design
- [`ms_size()`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/ms_size.md)
  : Number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up for a
  target power

## Methods

- [`print(`*`<ms_model>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_model.md)
  : Print an ms_model object
- [`print(`*`<ms_accrual>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_accrual.md)
  : Print an ms_accrual object
- [`print(`*`<ms_scenario>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_scenario.md)
  : Print an ms_scenario object
- [`print(`*`<ms_looks>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_looks.md)
  : Print an ms_looks object
- [`print(`*`<ms_test>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_test.md)
  : Print an ms_test object
- [`print(`*`<ms_power>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_power.md)
  : Print an ms_power object
- [`summary(`*`<ms_power>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/summary.ms_power.md)
  : Summarize an ms_power object
- [`print(`*`<summary.ms_power>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.summary.ms_power.md)
  : Print a summary.ms_power object
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<ms_power>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/as.data.frame.ms_power.md)
  : Per-look results of an ms_power object as a data frame
- [`print(`*`<ms_size>`*`)`](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/reference/print.ms_size.md)
  : Print an ms_size object
